newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKIA Q2 GDP DIPS SLIGHTLY TO 6.9 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKIA Q2 GDP DIPS SLIGHTLY TO 6.9 PERCENT.

text.p: Slovak second quarter gross
domestic product (GDP), in real terms, rose 6.9 percent
year-on-year, boosted by an 8.2 percent growth in household
consumption, the Statistical Bureau (SUSR) said on Wednesday.
In comparison, last year's second quarter GDP grew 7.1
percent, while household consumption rose 7.0 percent during
the same period, year-on-year, the SUSR said.
The Bureau said it had revised down the forecast for GDP
growth for the whole of 1996 to 7.0 percent from its previous
forecast of 7.1 percent.
Analysts said the latest figures were in line with
expectations, as the negative aspects of Slovakia's foreign
trade deficit of 31 billion crowns for the first seven months
of this year had to be taken into account.
"There is a danger that the GDP has been driven too much by
household consumption rather than other factors," Charlie
Robertson of London analysts Hilfe, told Reuters.
"It seems that there will be further pressure on the
central bank to help correct this," he added.
Real GDP in the first half of this year rose to 7.1
percent. GDP for the whole of 1995 grew by 7.4 percent and
household consumption for the whole year increased by 3.4
percent.
"I would say a figure of between six to seven percent GDP
growth is more realistic," Robertson said.
-- Bratislava Newsroom (42-7) 210 3687
